recall_prompt: Say what a conditional event is and how it is written, then say the conditional probability formula and the condition on P(A).
insider_note: Two definitions, two marks each. The formula mark needs the condition P(A) ≠ 0 written with it — it is part of the definition, not a footnote.

steps.label: Conditional event
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Name the two events, say that A has already occurred, and give the notation B|A.

lines.text: Conditional event: Let A, B be two events of a
sample space S. The event that B occurs, given
that A has already occurred, is called the
conditional event of B given A, denoted B|A.

recall.must_convey: That the conditional event B|A is the event of B occurring given that A has already occurred.
accept: the event that B occurs given that A has already occurred is the conditional event B given A
B after A has happened is the conditional event written B bar A
conditional event is the occurrence of B once A is known to have occurred
A jarigina tarvata B jaragadam ane event ni conditional event B given A antaru

steps.why: Once A is known to have happened, the outcomes outside A are ruled out; the conditional event is B seen inside that reduced set.
common_mistakes: Writing the formula and no words for the event itself.
Reversing the roles: A given B.

steps.label: Conditional probability
steps.margin_note: Two marks. The formula and its condition P(A) ≠ 0 together.

lines.text: Conditional probability: the probability of the
conditional event B|A is, for P(A) ≠ 0,

recall.must_convey: That the conditional probability of B given A is P(B|A) = P(A ∩ B)/P(A), defined when P(A) ≠ 0.
accept: P of B given A is P of A intersection B divided by P of A when P A is not zero
conditional probability equals the intersection over the probability of the given event
the formula is P A and B over P A with P A non zero
P B given A ante P A intersection B by P A, P A zero kakoodadu

steps.why: Within A, the only outcomes of B that can still occur are those in A ∩ B; dividing by P(A) rescales so that A itself has probability 1.
common_mistakes: Dividing by P(B) instead of P(A).
